items.stem: A prompt produces vague output. Which change most reliably improves it?

options.text: Add the missing constraint (audience, length, format)
options.rationale: Correct: supplying the missing constraint targets the gap rather than padding the prompt.

options.text: Repeat the same prompt several times
options.rationale: Repetition without change rarely improves quality.

options.text: Make the prompt much longer with synonyms
options.rationale: Length alone does not add the missing constraint.
The issue is the prompt, not the app.

items.explanation: Correct: supplying the missing constraint targets the gap rather than padding the prompt.

items.stem: Which TWO improve the relevance of a Microsoft 365 Copilot answer? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Referencing the specific document to ground the prompt
options.rationale: Correct: grounding in the right source improves relevance.

options.text: Stating the goal, audience and desired format
options.rationale: Correct: clear scope helps Copilot produce a relevant answer.

options.text: Trusting the first answer without review
options.rationale: Reviewing is still required; this does not improve relevance.

options.text: Removing all context so Copilot is free to guess

items.explanation: Correct: grounding in the right source improves relevance.

items.stem: A task needs a figure from a file the prompt never references. The best fix is to:

options.text: Ground the prompt by referencing that file
options.rationale: Correct: a data gap is solved by grounding, not by wordsmithing the prompt.
Politeness does not supply missing data.

options.text: Ask Copilot to invent a plausible figure
options.rationale: Inventing figures is unsafe and wrong.
Shortening does not supply the missing data.
